description: A blank ('') SEX value is a sex group of its own. Its average ratio counts in the first mean and can survive the cutoffs.

c.request: Matching lab tests to patients, average the CPK-to-GPT ratio for each `SEX` value, ignoring tests where the ratio is missing. Keep the sexes whose average is above the mean of those averages, then among them keep the ones above their own mean. In one unrounded row, give the average ratio of the sexes left, how far above the first mean they are on average, and how far above the second mean they are on average. A blank ('') SEX value is a sex group of its own. Its average ratio counts in the first mean and can survive the cutoffs.
c.sql: WITH lab_ratios AS (SELECT l.ID, p.SEX, CASE WHEN l.GPT IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT != 0 AND l.CPK IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(l.CPK AS FLOAT) / CAST(l.GPT AS FLOAT) ELSE NULL END AS ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID), sex_averages AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM lab_ratios WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SEX), first_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_val FROM sex_averages), filtered_sexes AS (SELECT sa.SEX FROM sex_averages sa CROSS JOIN first_mean fm WHERE sa.avg_ratio > fm.mean_val), filtered_records AS (SELECT lr.ratio, sa.avg_ratio, fm.mean_val FROM lab_ratios lr JOIN filtered_sexes fs ON lr.SEX = fs.SEX JOIN sex_averages sa ON lr.SEX = sa.SEX CROSS JOIN first_mean fm WHERE lr.ratio IS NOT NULL AND lr.ratio > sa.avg_ratio) SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio_remaining, AVG(ratio - mean_val) AS avg_above_first_mean, AVG(ratio - avg_ratio) AS avg_above_second_mean FROM filtered_records

d.request: For each SEX value (including blank '' as its own sex group), calculate the average CPK-to-GPT ratio from Laboratory tests matched to Patient records, ignoring missing ratios; compute the mean of these sex-level averages; retain only sex groups whose average exceeds this global mean; within each retained sex, filter to individual ratios above that sex's own average; output the mean of remaining ratios, its average distance above the global mean, and its average distance above each sex's respective mean.
d.sql: WITH base_ratios AS (SELECT p.SEX, CAST(l.CPK AS FLOAT) / CAST(l.GPT AS FLOAT) as ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.CPK IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT != 0), sex_averages AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(ratio) as sex_avg FROM base_ratios GROUP BY SEX), global_mean_calc AS (SELECT AVG(sex_avg) as global_mean FROM sex_averages), retained_sexes AS (SELECT SEX FROM sex_averages WHERE sex_avg > (SELECT global_mean FROM global_mean_calc)), filtered_ratios AS (SELECT br.ratio, sa.sex_avg, gm.global_mean FROM base_ratios br JOIN sex_averages sa ON br.SEX = sa.SEX CROSS JOIN global_mean_calc gm WHERE br.SEX IN (SELECT SEX FROM retained_sexes) AND br.ratio > sa.sex_avg) SELECT AVG(ratio) as mean_of_remaining_ratios, AVG(ratio) - (SELECT global_mean FROM global_mean_calc) as avg_distance_above_global_mean, AVG(ratio - sex_avg) as avg_distance_above_sex_mean FROM filtered_ratios

a.request: Join each lab test to its patient and compute the CPK ÷ GPT ratio per test, ignoring tests where the ratio is missing. Average the ratio separately for every distinct `SEX` value. Patients whose `SEX` is an empty string '' form a group of their own and are kept, and so do patients with a missing sex. Take the plain mean of all these group averages, blank group included, and keep the groups whose average is above it. Then take the mean of the kept groups' averages and keep the groups above that second mean. Return one unrounded row with: the average of the remaining groups' ratio averages, the average amount by which they exceed the first mean, and the average amount by which they exceed the second mean.
a.sql: WITH lab_with_ratio AS (SELECT p.SEX, CASE WHEN l.GPT IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT != 0 AND l.CPK IS NOT NULL THEN l.CPK * 1.0 / l.GPT ELSE NULL END as ratio FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID), sex_averages AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(ratio) as group_avg FROM lab_with_ratio WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SEX), first_mean AS (SELECT AVG(group_avg) as mean1 FROM sex_averages), above_first_mean AS (SELECT sa.SEX, sa.group_avg FROM sex_averages sa CROSS JOIN first_mean fm WHERE sa.group_avg > fm.mean1), second_mean AS (SELECT AVG(group_avg) as mean2 FROM above_first_mean), above_second_mean AS (SELECT abf.SEX, abf.group_avg FROM above_first_mean abf CROSS JOIN second_mean sm WHERE abf.group_avg > sm.mean2) SELECT AVG(group_avg) as final_avg, AVG(group_avg - (SELECT mean1 FROM first_mean)) as avg_exceed_first, AVG(group_avg - (SELECT mean2 FROM second_mean)) as avg_exceed_second FROM above_second_mean;

b.request: Calculate average CPK-to-GPT ratio per SEX group (including empty string as a distinct group) from joined Laboratory-Patient data, filter groups above the mean of all group averages, filter remaining groups above the mean of those filtered averages, and report the remaining groups' average ratio and their mean distances above both the first and second means.
b.sql:
WITH lab_patient_join AS (
  SELECT 
    l.CPK,
    l.GPT,
    COALESCE(p.SEX, '') as sex_group
  FROM Laboratory l
  JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
  WHERE l.CPK IS NOT NULL 
    AND l.GPT IS NOT NULL 
    AND l.GPT != 0
),
ratio_per_group AS (
  SELECT 
    sex_group,
    AVG(CAST(CPK AS FLOAT) / GPT) as avg_ratio
  FROM lab_patient_join
  GROUP BY sex_group
),
first_mean_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as first_mean
  FROM ratio_per_group
),
after_first_filter AS (
  SELECT 
    r.sex_group,
    r.avg_ratio,
    fm.first_mean
  FROM ratio_per_group r
  CROSS JOIN first_mean_calc fm
  WHERE r.avg_ratio > fm.first_mean
),
second_mean_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as second_mean
  FROM after_first_filter
),
final_groups AS (
  SELECT 
    af.sex_group,
    af.avg_ratio,
    af.first_mean,
    sm.second_mean
  FROM after_first_filter af
  CROSS JOIN second_mean_calc sm
  WHERE af.avg_ratio > sm.second_mean
)
SELECT 
  sex_group,
  avg_ratio,
  avg_ratio - first_mean as distance_above_first_mean,
  avg_ratio - second_mean as distance_above_second_mean
FROM final_groups;
b.raw: Calculate average CPK-to-GPT ratio per SEX group (including empty string as a distinct group) from joined Laboratory-Patient data, filter groups above the mean of all group averages, filter remaining groups above the mean of those filtered averages, and report the remaining groups' average ratio and their mean distances above both the first and second means.
